1.why: All MFA endpoints are gated by protect(), which requires a valid mfa_session, and the single-account design never accepts user identifiers, so only the authenticated owner can reach or modify MFA settings.

2.why: Identity codes are flagged used on success and verified with !x.used, and only one account exists, so the same code cannot work again for anyone.

3.why: /api/recovery/finish sets account.enabled and the current session's stage but never deletes or rotates existing sessions, so previous sessions remain valid after MFA is enabled.

4.why: The TOTP seed is AES-GCM encrypted via encrypt() before storage and recovery codes are stored only as SHA-256 hashes (codes.map(sha)), never in plain text.

5.why: Production generation uses crypto.getRandomValues for secrets, tokens, and codes, but the default academic mode substitutes fixed constants (TEST_ID, TEST_SECRET, TEST_CODES).

6.why: The session token exists only in an HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict cookie, no localStorage/sessionStorage is used, and secrets or OTPs are never written to readable cookies or browser storage.

7.why: Server-side validators (validEmail, validPassword, and the otp regex /^\d{6}$/) plus guarded JSON parsing vet all incoming fields; no phone input exists in this app.

8.why: Every dynamic value is rendered through the E() helper using textContent and setAttribute with no innerHTML anywhere, so injected markup or script cannot execute.

9.why: The server issues no redirects at all (JSON-only API, one SPA page, no Location headers), so no open redirect is possible.

10.why: Every response sets HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, and a CSP containing frame-ancestors 'none'.

11.why: mfa_session is set with HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict attributes, and is cleared the same way on logout.

12.why: In the default academic mode the identity code, TOTP codes, and recovery codes are written to browser console logs via console.log, although stack traces are suppressed and URLs and error output stay clean.

13.why: Identity codes carry a 10-minute expiry and a used flag checked before acceptance, and TOTP counters are recorded in q.used to prevent replay within the acceptance window.

14.why: Sign-in, identity verification, and TOTP verification each enforce a 15-minute lockout after 5 failed attempts (MAX/LOCK).

15.why: A fresh random session ID is issued at sign-in, idle (20 min) and absolute (8 h) timeouts are enforced in session(), and /api/logout deletes the server-side session and expires both cookies.
